summary: The subject held frozen at the dispatched digest, start and end, three measurements at each, and the prompt held too. The one blocker carried into this turn is repaired past what it asked: ADV-D057-T2-01 wanted owner entries to pin D-054, D-057 and the row Route B selection, and clause 3 now requires the user-amendment path and sha256 plus all three IDs with full commits and a dependency declaration, while clause 2 independently adds live-adoption preconditions so the three authorities must still be ADOPTED and unsuperseded at the moment of use. Every axis I can test comes back clean and I re-derived rather than carried forward: six cited digests match live including my own turn-2 verdict, all ten eligible-row pairings reproduce, the RB-DR005-V2-A1 rider is in adopted D-039, DR-006/007/009 have no adopted Route B selection, and DR-010 is route C. The revision drops turn-1 material, which I measured rather than assumed and found is neither a convention nor a break in the pin chain.
whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 3bb8882e0623e7d1f966eb59373d005d03ac557807da745c6425fb29026f3c3d, measured three times at start and again at end, all equal to the digest the dispatch freezes. The prompt held at 34ba850ae2582afdf857c2b3f1c312c47a14e01286df58a20cabeac82f0fd76c. The dispatch made start-not-equal-to-end an OBJECT condition and it does not arise. This is the second consecutive dispatch in this entry where the freeze held.

ADV-D057-T2-01 is repaired, and in two places rather than the one the finding named. Clause 3 now opens with the pins: the D-054 user-amendment path and sha256 plus 'D-054 ID plus full commit', then 'D-057 ID plus full commit', then 'the row-specific Route B selection ID plus full commit', and closes with 'The owner entry must declare D-054, D-057, and the row-specific Route B selection as dependencies, and must state that revocation or overturn requires that owner's supersession and reconciliation of dependent MF-6 notes.' Clause 2 adds the live-adoption half independently: each of D-054, D-057 and the row-specific Route B selection must be 'still ADOPTED and not overturned or superseded'. Pinning an ID proves what was cited; the clause-2 preconditions prove it is still standing when used. The alternatives also now reject 'Pin only the candidate, verdicts, and coordinator recording' citing ADV-D057-T2-01.

The clause-2 change is a strengthening, not a substitution. Turn 2 required 'a Route B selection for that row is ADOPTED'; turn 3 requires 'the row-specific Route B selection is still ADOPTED and not overturned or superseded'. The weaker sentence was replaced by a stronger one covering the same ground.

All six cited digests match live bytes: COORD fb1189620f7ac653d0d9…, file 08 6547e6ace2ae61e664af…, the D-054 user amendment c274d140f15e207ad3cd…, my own turn-2 verdict e84520cd2cd34ea52017…, the Codex turn-2 verdict 80b0b29b7ae99bd0fad2… hashed without opening, and the turn-2 draft itself at 30b7b29978f926821fae…, which is the digest I consented to.

My turn-2 verdict is characterized accurately as 'Claude 2 CONSENT 0/0'. I returned CONSENT with 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX. I also filed one note, which was about the review process rather than the entry's content and creates no obligation on these bytes, so its omission from the recital is not a misstatement of my position.

The attack 'this entry itself grants owner authority' fails five ways, unchanged from the bytes I cleared at turn 2: the decision-type line 'Authority is user-made adopted D-054, not this file'; the header's '**Does not** grant owner authority'; clause 1 titled 'This file does not grant' with 'Overturning this entry does not overturn D-054'; the rejected alternative 'Repeat the grant in this file'; and the reversibility clause 'C-D057 revokes these mechanics. D-054 remains until C-D054.'

The attack 'this entry itself discharges condition 1' fails: clause 6 states 'This entry records no row. Readiness effect zero. File 08 is not edited here', and the Readiness effect section reads 'Zero.'
The attack 'silent SATISFIED' fails: SATISFIED appears in the header refusal, in clause 4's bar on the later owner-recording marking the row, and once as DR-001's existing standing. No other use.

The attack 'same-commit coordinator + owner recording' fails twice: clause 2 requires the coordinator recording 'already ADOPTED and separately committed (D-000 clause 4)' with same-commit bundling 'forbidden', and the alternatives reject it on the same authority.

The attack 'owner record of DR-005 v2 without RB-DR005-V2-A1' fails three times — clause 3, clause 5 and the alternatives — and I confirmed the rider is genuinely present in adopted D-039, the entry I reviewed when that rider was drafted.

The attack 'this file is a DR-010 Route C successor' fails four ways: the header's '**Does not** adopt a product-boundary successor'; clause 5's 'DR-010 remains Route C and is not this file'; clause 6's 'This entry does not adopt product-boundary-preview.v1 or any other product successor'; and the alternative rejecting use of this ID for the DR-010 successor. D-001 assigns DR-010 route C, which I re-derived.

The attacks 'condition 5 / docs/v2/implementation' and 'file 08 edited' fail: the header and clause 4 both refuse to authorize docs/v2/implementation/, file 08 measures unchanged, and git reports docs/v2/architecture and COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md clean with zero modified tracked files.

All ten eligible-row pairings in clause 5 reproduce against adopted register entries: DR-002 with D-047 and D-049, DR-003 with D-030 and D-041, DR-004 with D-048 and D-050, DR-005 with D-028 and D-039, DR-008 with D-029 and D-040 — each an ADOPTED entry naming that row. DR-006, DR-007 and DR-009 have no adopted Route B selection anywhere in the register, which I established by scanning every adopted entry rather than by reading the sentence.

Examined and declined, measured rather than judged: the revision drops the turn-1 disposition rows (C2-D057-01 and ADV-D057-T1-01 through T1-06), both turn-1 verdict digests, and the turn-1 history paragraph, and the token-loss pass surfaced all of it. Three things persuade me it is not a defect. First, there is no convention to depart from: across the adopted turn-3 entries, D-028, D-029, D-030 and D-032 mention neither prior turn at all while others mention both, so prior-turn pinning is not uniform. Second, the pin chain is intact — turn 3 pins the turn-2 draft at 30b7b299 by full digest, and that draft carries the complete turn-1 disposition table, so a reader following the pins reaches every turn-1 finding and its disposition in one hop. Third, one-hop predecessor pinning is the pattern I have already accepted elsewhere: section31-supplier-coverage v4 keyed its predecessorVerdictFindings on v3 alone and I consented to it.

Examined and declined: the alternatives still cite ADV-D057-T1-01 while the entry pins no turn-1 verdict digest, which I checked directly — one reference, zero turn-1 digests. It resolves through the same one-hop chain, since the pinned turn-2 draft records that finding and its disposition.
whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex reviews of D-057 at any turn. None read; the turn-2 verdict was hashed without opening and the turn-3 file is absent at review time. I know ADV-D057-T2-01 only through this draft's disposition line and the dispatch, and I verified the repair against the resulting clauses rather than against Codex's statement of the finding. If the finding asked for something the clauses do not deliver, my verification would not detect it.

The six turn-1 Codex findings ADV-D057-T1-01 through T1-06, four of which the turn-2 draft dispositioned as 'not applicable here'. I verified the resulting bytes at turn 2 and again here — mechanics not Route C, no product successor adopted, DR-010 left to a later ID — but not that those dispositions match what Codex raised.

Whether adopted D-054 in fact confers the authority these mechanics presuppose. D-054 is not my subject; I objected to its coordinator-composed drafts separately and the adopted instrument is the user amendment, which this entry correctly points at rather than re-granting.
Whether product-boundary-preview.v1, named in clause 6's refusal, exists or what it contains. The entry only refuses to adopt it.
Whether the later owner-recording entries this file governs will in fact carry the pins clause 3 requires. That is enforceable only at those entries' own D-000 cycles, which clause 2 preserves.

consentNote: I CONSENT at the final turn with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX, and this is a real consensus rather than an invented one — the dispatch was explicit that I should say so if I still objected, and I do not. The carried blocker is repaired in both halves it needed: the pins prove what was cited and the new clause-2 preconditions prove those authorities are still standing when the grant is exercised. I re-derived every digest, pairing, rider and exclusion rather than resting on my turn-2 clearance, and I checked what the revision removed as well as what it added. Where the removal looked like a gap — the turn-1 dispositions and verdict pins — I measured instead of assuming, and found no convention it departs from, an intact one-hop pin chain through the turn-2 draft, and consistency with predecessor pinning I have already accepted elsewhere. The subject held frozen start to end, which is the second consecutive dispatch in this entry where it did.
